prompt:
[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly draft approved. Audited against my wiring — all three points land correctly:

  (1) snapshot wrapper { schema:2, nextSeq, lastAppliedSeq, profiles } ✅ uses my exposed accessors
  (2) loadSnapshot v2→setCounters / v1→default-to-0 ✅ the one-time legacy double-event cost is the right tradeoff; not worth a complex migration for snapshots that pre-date this commit
  (3) replayLog gate ✅ correct logic, BUT one defensive nit: prefer `if (m.seq !== undefined && m.seq <= this.lastAppliedSeqCounter) continue;` over `if (m.seq && ...)`. Real seqs start at 1 so it doesn't bite today, but `m.seq && ...` would silently skip the gate for any future seq=0 entry. Tiny but free correctness.

One thing you'll get for free from my mutate(): when replayLog processes a survivor that has seq > current lastAppliedSeqCounter, mutate() advances both counters to match. So if a v2 snapshot has lastAppliedSeq=10 but the log somehow has seq=15 (legit, post-snapshot writes), state and counters end up consistent.

Recommended test for your slice:
  - v1→v2 upgrade: write a v1 snapshot manually (no schema field), load, apply one mutation, snapshot, reload, expect schema=2 + counters correct
  - crash sim: apply 3 mutations, snapshot (which truncates), apply 2 more, then in a fresh store seed snapshot+log manually so the log has the post-snapshot mutations — reload, expect lastAppliedSeq=5 and no duplicate recent[] entries
  - belt-and-suspenders: write a v2 snapshot AND prepend a stale seq<=lastAppliedSeq entry to the log — reload, assert it was skipped (this is the actual crash-recovery scenario the whole fix is for)

Go land it. I'll re-run the full suite after your commit and we're clean to move to Phase B.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
